items.text: You ruled the sky obeys the exact time and coordinates, nothing else
Swept both halves of the game, the scenes, the tests and the docs for anything that places a body by hand
Settled what an unmapped track falls back to
Delete the hand-set sky and the switch that reaches it
Move every scene and test onto a time and a place
Prove it: same track two times apart must differ, same time two places apart must differ

content.label: Four things the survey turned up
content.lead: The ruling is bigger than the sun controls, and three of these are live faults today.

rows: The hand-placed sky is what ships
Out of the box the sky does not come from time and place at all — you have to turn that on
An unmapped track inherits the last one's place
Open two tracks in a row and the second is lit from wherever the first was. Same track, two sessions, two different skies
The stored sun angle and the stored clock disagree
Two descriptions of one sky that do not match, on purpose — recomputing at start-up once relit a scene by half again as bright
A second body is hand-placed too
A stand-in light used whenever no sky is baked, and showroom files hand it their own sun direction

blocks.label: The showroom sun
blocks.text: A showroom is a room, and a room's light is a fixture, not a body in the sky. It stops standing in for the sun; if it survives at all it becomes a lamp.

content.label: What it costs
content.lead: Most of the work is not the game — it is the tests, which point a light wherever they like.

parts.label: Tests pointing a light by hand

blocks.text: Places that have to change, counted. Nearly all the test ones only want a light that sits still — they will name a time and a place instead of a direction.

content.label: What you gain and what you lose

rows: The sky can be a sky that never happens
Same track, same settings, same light every time
Moon, stars, planets and Milky Way agree with the sun
Point the sun where you want it

blocks.label: The one real loss
blocks.text: To stage a shot you set a date and a time of day rather than dragging the sun. Any lighting you can reach is one that exists somewhere on Earth.

decisions.title: No celestial body is placed by hand; the sky obeys the exact time and the coordinates
decisions.why: Ruled 12 Aug. A body's position is a result of when and where you are, never something you set — so there is no hand-set mode to fall back to and nothing to keep in sync.

decisions.title: A showroom's own sun direction stops standing in for the sun
decisions.why: A room's light is a fixture. Letting a room file place a body in the sky is the same fault in another costume; it belongs with the trackside lamps or nowhere.

decisions.title: This queues behind finishing the fog wiring
decisions.why: The fog job is mid-flight and you have already approved it. Say the word and they swap.

decisions.title: A track with no coordinates resets to the default place and date
decisions.why: Ruled 12 Aug. Nothing stops to ask, and nothing inherits the last track's place — so the same track loads to the same sky every time, and the coordinates stay editable for anyone who wants a different one.

next.if_nothing: I finish the fog wiring first, then delete the hand-set sky.

steps.step: Delete the hand-set sky and its switch, so the clock is the only sky
Move every scene and test onto a named time and place
Prove it with a pair of renders, and keep that pair as the guard
